transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a draft sustainability-linked bond on the table today — a five-year, $50 million issue targeted at institutional investors. As is our standard process, I'd like to hear from each relevant function before I make my final approval and structuring decision. Let's start with the sustainability team's assessment, then move to treasury, legal, and compliance. Please walk me through your reviews, including any concerns about the coupon step-up provisions, hedge amounts, and post-issuance reporting controls you see in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical legal issue before we proceed. I completed a board-resolution review this morning and found that the authorized principal for this issue is exactly $42,000,000 — not $50,000,000. The current draft exceeds our board authorization by $8,000,000. My note on this has not yet been circulated, but Elena, you cannot sign off on a $50 million issue without either amending the draft to $42 million or obtaining new board authorization for the higher amount.

transcript.text: I received the verified KPI methodology from our sustainability auditor this week. Based on that review, the bond can retain its sustainability-linked structure only with a 30-basis-point coupon step-up for a missed target and an annual external-assurance report. The current draft doesn't specify a coupon step-up, hedge amount, or post-issuance reporting controls, so it will need to be amended to include these provisions before it can validly carry the sustainability-linked label.

I confirmed this morning that our refinancing schedule requires a seven-year maturity for this issue, not the five-year term currently in the draft. Additionally, the bank has approved swap capacity to hedge exactly 75% of a $42,000,000 issue, which comes to $31,500,000.
